documents.title: Academic Regulations 2024
documents.issuer: Office of the Dean of Academics

sections.title: Academic year
sections.text: The academic year has two regular semesters, Fall and Winter, of about 18 weeks each, followed by an optional summer term for re-registering failed courses.

sections.title: Credits
sections.text: Each course carries between 1 and 4 credits. Students must register for 16 to 27 credits per semester. A lighter load needs approval from the Dean of Academics.

sections.title: Minimum attendance
sections.text: Students must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in every course, counted from the first day of instruction to the last instructional day. Theory and laboratory attendance are calculated separately.

sections.title: Condonation
sections.text: Students whose attendance falls short of the minimum because of documented medical reasons may apply for condonation of up to 10% through the Head of Department, within one week of the attendance cut-off date.

sections.title: Debarment
sections.text: Students below the minimum attendance requirement in a course are debarred from writing the Final Assessment Test (FAT) of that course and must re-register for it.

sections.title: Continuous Assessment Tests
sections.text: Each theory course has two Continuous Assessment Tests, CAT-1 and CAT-2, each conducted for 50 marks and scaled to 15% of the course total. Digital assignments and quizzes make up a further 30%.

sections.title: Final Assessment Test
sections.text: The Final Assessment Test (FAT) is held at the end of the semester for 100 marks and scaled to 40% of the course total. FAT dates are published by the Controller of Examinations.

sections.title: FAT eligibility
sections.text: A student may write the FAT of a course only if they meet the minimum attendance requirement and have attempted at least one of the two CATs. Hall tickets are issued only to eligible students.

sections.title: Passing a course
sections.text: To pass a course, a student must score at least 50 out of 100 in the overall course total and at least 40 out of 100 in the FAT.

sections.title: Grades
sections.text: Grades are awarded as S (91–100), A (81–90), B (71–80), C (61–70), D (55–60), E (50–54) and F (below 50 or absent). Grade points run from 10 for S down to 0 for F.

sections.title: Re-examination
sections.text: Students who fail a course, or miss the FAT for a valid reason, may apply for re-examination within five days of the results. A re-examination fee applies per course.

sections.title: Academic integrity
sections.text: Malpractice in any assessment, including the use of unauthorised material or devices, leads to cancellation of that assessment and may lead to suspension.

sections.title: Fee payment
sections.text: Semester fees must be paid before the registration deadline. A late fee of ₹1,000 per week applies for up to three weeks, after which the registration is cancelled.

sections.title: Library hours
sections.text: The central library is open from 8 am to 8 pm on weekdays and from 9 am to 5 pm on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays.

sections.title: Hall tickets
sections.text: Hall tickets are released on the student portal one week before the FAT. Students without a hall ticket are not admitted to the examination hall.

sections.title: Reporting time
sections.text: Students must be seated 15 minutes before each exam starts. Late entry is allowed for the first 30 minutes only.

sections.title: Permitted items
sections.text: Only a transparent pouch, pens and an approved non-programmable calculator are permitted. Mobile phones and smart watches must be left outside the hall.

sections.title: Make-up tests
sections.text: Make-up tests for a missed CAT are held only for students with approved medical or official leave, within two weeks of the missed test.

sections.title: Results and re-evaluation
sections.text: FAT results are published on the portal within three weeks of the last exam. Students can request a re-evaluation within five days of the results.

sections.title: FAT schedule
sections.text: The Winter 2026 FAT schedule runs for three weeks starting 17 November. Timetables are released department by department.

sections.title: In-time
sections.text: Residents must return to the hostel by 9:30 pm every day. Late entries are recorded, and repeated late entries are reported to parents.

sections.title: Visitors
sections.text: Visitors are allowed in the hostel lobby from 4 pm to 7 pm. Visitors are not permitted inside rooms.

sections.title: Mess timings
sections.text: Breakfast is served from 7 to 9 am, lunch from 12 to 2 pm and dinner from 7:30 to 9:30 pm.

sections.title: Leave
sections.text: Residents going home must apply for leave on the hostel portal at least one day in advance and get the warden's approval.

sections.title: Room maintenance
sections.text: Maintenance requests are raised on the hostel portal and are usually resolved within 48 hours.

documents.title: CSE Department Handbook
documents.issuer: Department of Computer Science and Engineering

sections.title: Lab records
sections.text: Lab records must be submitted every week and are evaluated as part of the laboratory component. Late submissions lose 10% of the marks for that experiment.

sections.title: Project reviews
sections.text: Mini-project reviews happen in weeks 6, 10 and 14 of the semester. Each review is evaluated by a two-member faculty panel.

sections.title: Faculty advisors
sections.text: Every student is assigned a faculty advisor who approves course registration and can be met during posted office hours.

sections.title: Attendance requirement
sections.text: With effect from the Winter 2025 semester, the minimum attendance requirement for all CSE courses is 80%. The university's condonation rules continue to apply.

sections.title: Laboratory attendance
sections.text: Laboratory attendance is counted separately from theory and must also be at least 80% for CSE students.

sections.title: Effect on the regulations
sections.text: This circular supersedes clause 3.1 of the Academic Regulations 2024 for students of the Department of CSE.
